Sweeping a diffusion or an opinion dynamic over its settings

Source: R/interpret_sweeps.R
sweep.Rd

sweep_diffusion() plays manynet::play_diffusion(), and sweep_opinion() plays manynet::play_opinion(), times times for each setting of the arguments in vary, to show how the result changes with them: for example, the share of the network infected for each chance of transmission, or the number of opinion clusters for each confidence.

A sweep explores a model. To compare a model with an observed diffusion, or two models with each other, use play_diffusions() with test_gof() or test_distributions().

Usage

sweep_diffusion(.data, ..., vary, times = 5, control = list())

sweep_opinion(.data, opinions, ..., vary, times = 5, control = list())

# S3 method for class 'diffusionSweep'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'opinionSweep'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

.data

A network of a manynet-consistent class, such as a matrix, an edgelist, an igraph, a network, a tbl_graph, or a stocnet object.

...

Other arguments of manynet::play_diffusion() or manynet::play_opinion(), which are the same in every setting, such as steps or rule.

vary

A named list of the values to try for one or more arguments, such as list(transmissibility = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5)). Each value of a vector is one setting. For a setting that is itself a vector, such as a set of seeds, give a list: list(seeds = list(1:10, 1:20)). A named list names its settings: list(seeds = list(hub = 1, edge = 5)). With more than one argument, every combination of their values is played.

times

The number of runs for each setting. By default 5. A model without chance, such as a diffusion with a transmissibility of 1, or the DeGroot or Hegselmann–Krause rule, gives the same result in every run.

control

The controls of the runs, as a named list such as list(ncores = 4, seed = 1). It reads ncores, strategy, and seed. The same seed gives the same runs sequentially and in parallel. A control that is not named keeps its default, or the value set with set_control_computation().

opinions

For sweep_opinion(), the opinions at the start, as in manynet::play_opinion(): one value for each node, or the name of a node attribute. Give several sets of opinions in vary instead, as vary = list(opinions = list(...)).

object

A diffusionSweep or an opinionSweep.

Value

A table with a column first for each argument in vary, and the run in sim. Each column of a setting holds the value of the setting where each value is one number or string, the names of a named list, the number of seeds for a list of seeds, and otherwise the place of the setting.

sweep_diffusion() returns a diffusionSweep, with one row for each step of each run, and the counts of manynet::as_diffusion(). Its summary() gives, for each setting and run, the share of the nodes that were infected (infected, which counts a node again where it is reinfected), and the steps until every node adopted (toa), which is NA where not every node adopted.

sweep_opinion() returns an opinionSweep, with one row for each run: the number of opinion clusters at the end, whether they reach a consensus, the spread (standard deviation) and mean of the opinions at the end, the number of steps played, and whether the opinions settled before the last step. Two opinions are in one cluster where they are within 0.01 of each other, or of an opinion between them.

print() gives the mean of each for each setting, and returns x, invisibly. plot() from {autograph} draws the result against the first argument in vary.

See also

Other interpreting functions: play_diffusions(), predict_mrqap, simulate_mrqap

Examples

# The share infected for three chances of transmission
sweep_diffusion(ison_adolescents, steps = 10,
                vary = list(transmissibility = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5)),
                control = list(seed = 1))
#> # 15 simulated diffusions over 3 settings of transmissibility
#> 
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   transmissibility infected complete   toa
#>              <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1              0.1    0.275      0    NA  
#> 2              0.3    0.75       0.4  10  
#> 3              0.5    1          1     7.6
#> 
#> # For each setting: the mean share infected, the share of runs in which every
#> #   node adopted, and their mean steps until then.
#> # Controls: seed = 1
# The number of opinion clusters for three widths of confidence
set.seed(1)
sweep_opinion(ison_networkers, stats::runif(32), rule = "hegselmann_krause",
              vary = list(confidence = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)), times = 1)
#> # 3 simulated opinion dynamics over 3 settings of confidence
#> 
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   confidence clusters consensus spread settled
#>        <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1        0.1        8         0 0.276        0
#> 2        0.2        3         0 0.195        1
#> 3        0.3        2         0 0.0854       1
#> 
#> # For each setting: the mean number of clusters at the end, and the share of
#> #   runs that reach a consensus or settle.
